name: Deputy
description: Deputy workforce management: employees, locations and areas, rosters (shifts) and publishing, timesheets with clock on and off and approval, leave and unavailability, memos and the resource query API. Per-install Deputy API with a permanent token.
prerequisites: A Deputy system administrator who can open the install's OAuth clients page to create a permanent token.

DEPUTY_HOST.label: Install address
DEPUTY_HOST.help: The host name of your Deputy install, as shown in the browser when you are logged in: <install>.<region>.deputy.com, e.g. mycompany.au.deputy.com or mycompany.na.deputy.com. Without https:// and without a path.
DEPUTY_HOST.patternMessage: Enter only the host, e.g. mycompany.au.deputy.com, without https:// or /api.

DEPUTY_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Permanent token
DEPUTY_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: https://<install>.<region>.deputy.com/exec/devapp/oauth_clients: add an OAuth client, then click Get an Access Token. The token is shown only once.
DEPUTY_ACCESS_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste only the token, without Bearer, spaces or quotes.

verifyHints.401: Deputy refused the token. Check that it belongs to this install (tokens work only on the install that issued them) or create a new one on the install's OAuth clients page.
verifyHints.403: The token's user lacks the permission for this call. Use a token of a system administrator or a manager covering the locations you read.
verifyHints.404: The install address or the endpoint was not found. Check DEPUTY_HOST, e.g. mycompany.au.deputy.com.

instructions:
## Deputy
This connector reads and updates a **Deputy** install through its API (`https://<install>.<region>.deputy.com/api/v1`): employees, locations and areas, rosters (shifts), timesheets, leave, unavailability, memos and any other record through Deputy's resource query API.

**Personal data**: employee records hold names, dates of birth, contact details, addresses and pay data. Read only what the task needs.

**Setup (5 minutes, needs a Deputy system administrator)**
1. Note your install address from the browser bar when logged in, e.g. `mycompany.au.deputy.com` (regions: `au`, `eu`, `uk`, `na` for the US). Put it into `DEPUTY_HOST` without `https://`.
2. Open `https://<your install address>/exec/devapp/oauth_clients`, add an OAuth client (name and any description; the client id itself is not used), then click **Get an Access Token**.
3. Copy the permanent token at once (it is shown only once) into `DEPUTY_ACCESS_TOKEN`. It works only on this install and acts as the user who created it, with that user's permissions; a system administrator sees every location. `deputy_get_me` is the install check.

**Words**: Deputy calls a location (workplace) a *Company*, an area (department) an *OperationalUnit*, a shift a *Roster* and actual worked time a *Timesheet*. A leave type is a *LeaveRules* record.

**Workflow**
- Who am I: `deputy_get_me`. The token user's own data: `deputy_get_my_rosters`, `deputy_get_my_timesheets`, `deputy_get_my_leave`, `deputy_get_my_unavailability`, `deputy_get_my_locations`, `deputy_get_my_colleagues`.
- Structure: `deputy_list_locations` (ids are the location ids), `deputy_list_areas` (each area belongs to a location; shifts and timesheets use area ids).
- People: `deputy_list_employees`, `deputy_get_employee`, `deputy_query_employees` for filters, `deputy_get_employee_shift_status` for who is working now.
- Schedule: `deputy_list_rosters` covers 12 hours back to 36 hours ahead; `deputy_query_rosters` for any period (filter on `Date`, `Employee`, `OperationalUnit`). To plan: `deputy_save_shift` (new or, with `roster_id`, update), `deputy_copy_rosters` (repeat last week), `deputy_publish_rosters` (choose the notification).
- Time: `deputy_query_timesheets`, `deputy_get_timesheet`. Clock on and off: `deputy_start_timesheet`, `deputy_pause_timesheet`, `deputy_end_timesheet`. Fix or add a past timesheet: `deputy_save_timesheet`. Approve for payroll: `deputy_approve_timesheet` (approvals of time).
- Leave: `deputy_query_leave`, `deputy_get_employee_leave`; leave types with `deputy_query_resource` and `object` `LeaveRules`. Book with `deputy_add_leave`; approve, decline or cancel with `deputy_update_leave` (`status` 1, 2 or 3).
- Availability: `deputy_get_employee_unavailability`, `deputy_query_availability`, `deputy_add_unavailability`.
- Employees: `deputy_add_employee`, `deputy_update_employee`, `deputy_invite_employee`, `deputy_terminate_employee` (reversible) and `deputy_reactivate_employee`. Manager notes: `deputy_post_journal`. News feed: `deputy_post_memo`.
- Anything else (teams, public holidays, events, training, custom fields, sales data, pay periods): `deputy_get_resource_info` lists an object's fields, `deputy_query_resource` searches it, `deputy_get_resource` reads one record.

**Switched off at install**: `deputy_delete_employee`, `deputy_discard_rosters` and `deputy_discard_timesheet`; they cannot be undone, so an admin switches them on when the team needs them.

**Query tools** (`deputy_query_*` and `deputy_query_resource`) send POST but only read. Body: `search` with clauses `{"s1":{"field":"Date","type":"ge","data":"2026-11-01"},"s2":{"field":"Date","type":"le","data":"2026-11-07"}}` (all must match; operators eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, in, not in, starts, contains, is, is not), `sort` (`{"Date":"asc"}`), `join` (`["EmployeeObject"]`) and paging.

**Reading the answers**
- Ids are integers. `StartTime` / `EndTime` and the `start` / `end` inputs are **Unix timestamps in seconds**; `Date` fields are local dates of the location (`2026-11-03T00:00:00+11:00`). Convert with the location's time zone.
- Roster `Employee` 0 is an open shift; `Published` false is a draft. Timesheet `TimeApproved`, `PayRuleApproved`, `Discarded`, `IsInProgress` give the state; `TotalTime` is hours.
- Leave `Status`: 0 awaiting approval, 1 approved, 2 declined, 3 cancelled, 4 pay approved.
- Adding or updating a shift answers 200 with an empty body; check with `deputy_query_rosters`.

**Paging**: an answer holds at most 500 records. Query tools take `max` (up to 500) and `start` (offset); when a page is full, call again with `start` raised by `max`. The list tools without paging return everything Deputy allows in one answer.

**Errors**: 401 means a wrong token or a token of another install, 403 a missing permission of the token's user, 404 a wrong install address or record id, 400 a bad field name in a filter (check `deputy_get_resource_info`).

tools.name: deputy_get_me
tools.description: Who the token belongs to: user and employee id, name, company (location) ids, permissions and the install's settings. The install check.

tools.name: deputy_get_my_rosters
tools.description: Upcoming shifts of the token's own user (when am I next working), with times, area and location.

tools.name: deputy_get_my_timesheets
tools.description: Timesheets of the token's own user, newest first, with start and end times, breaks and approval state.

tools.name: deputy_get_my_leave
tools.description: Leave requests of the token's own user, with dates, leave type, hours and status.

tools.name: deputy_get_my_unavailability
tools.description: Unavailability periods the token's own user has entered (when am I unavailable).

tools.name: deputy_get_my_locations
tools.description: Locations (workplaces) the token's own user can work in, with their areas.

tools.name: deputy_get_my_colleagues
tools.description: Colleagues of the token's own user (who do I work with): names, photos and contact details shared in Deputy.

tools.name: deputy_list_employees
tools.description: All employees the token may see, with id, name, main location (Company), role, active flag, start date, contact and payroll id. Contains personal data.

tools.name: deputy_get_employee
tools.description: One employee by id: name, locations, role, contact details, start and termination date, payroll id.

employee_id.description: Employee id (Id from deputy_list_employees, not the user id).

tools.name: deputy_query_employees
tools.description: Search employees with filters, sorting and paging, e.g. active staff of one location: search {"s1":{"field":"Active","type":"eq","data":true},"s2":{"field":"Company","type":"eq","data":1}}. A read: it sends POST but changes nothing.

search.description: Filter clauses keyed by any label: {"s1":{"field":"Date","type":"ge","data":"2026-11-01"},"s2":{"field":"Employee","type":"eq","data":12}}. Operators: eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, in, not in, starts, contains, is, is not (for null); field names are the resource's (see deputy_get_resource_info). All clauses must match. Omit for no filter.

sort.description: Sort, field name to asc or desc, e.g. {"Date":"desc"}.

start.description: Offset of the first record (0 based) for the next page: the previous start plus max.

join.description: Related objects to embed, e.g. ["EmployeeObject","OperationalUnitObject"]. Names end in Object.

tools.name: deputy_get_employee_shift_status
tools.description: Whether an employee is working right now: current or next shift, open timesheet and break state.

tools.name: deputy_list_locations
tools.description: All locations (Deputy calls them Company records: workplaces with name, code, address id, time zone and active flag). The id is the location id used everywhere else.

tools.name: deputy_list_areas
tools.description: All areas (operational units / departments) with name, location (Company), colour and active flag. Shifts and timesheets belong to an area.

tools.name: deputy_list_rosters
tools.description: Shifts (rosters) from 12 hours ago to 36 hours ahead across the install: employee, area, start and end (Unix seconds), published flag. For other ranges use deputy_query_rosters.

tools.name: deputy_query_rosters
tools.description: Search shifts (rosters) for any period, employee or area, e.g. one day: search {"s1":{"field":"Date","type":"eq","data":"2026-11-03"}}; a week: Date ge and Date le. Open shifts have Employee 0. A read: POST that changes nothing.

tools.description: Leave requests of one employee with dates, type, hours and status.

tools.name: deputy_get_employee_unavailability
tools.description: Unavailability periods of one employee (one-off and recurring), with start, end and comment.

tools.name: deputy_query_availability
tools.description: Search availability and unavailability records of employees (EmployeeAvailability): employee, start and end (Unix seconds), type and recurrence. A read: POST that changes nothing.

tools.name: deputy_get_resource
tools.description: Read one record of any Deputy resource by id, e.g. a Roster, Leave, LeaveRules or Company record.

tools.name: deputy_get_resource_info
tools.description: Field list of a Deputy resource: field names and types, and the joinable related objects. Use it to write search filters.

tools.name: deputy_add_employee
tools.description: Add an employee to a location. Returns the new employee record; invite them with deputy_invite_employee.

gender.description: 0 prefer not to say, 1 male, 2 female, 3 non-binary.

country_code.description: Country code for the address, e.g. AU, GB, US.

tools.name: deputy_update_employee
tools.description: Change fields of an employee record through the resource API. Only the fields sent change.

fields.description: Employee fields to set, named as in deputy_get_resource_info for Employee, e.g. {"FirstName":"Ana","DisplayName":"Ana P","Company":2,"Role":50,"StartDate":"2026-11-01"}.

tools.name: deputy_invite_employee
tools.description: Email the employee an invitation to log in to Deputy and use the app (sends a message).

tools.name: deputy_terminate_employee
tools.description: Terminate an employee: they can no longer log in or be rostered. Reversible with deputy_reactivate_employee.

tools.name: deputy_reactivate_employee
tools.description: Re-activate a terminated employee so they can be rostered again.

tools.name: deputy_delete_employee
tools.description: Delete an employee's account and data from Deputy. Cannot be undone; switched off at install.

tools.name: deputy_post_journal
tools.description: Add a journal entry (a private manager note) to an employee's profile.

tools.name: deputy_add_leave
tools.description: Create a leave request for an employee. Status 0 waits for manager approval; 1 records leave that is already approved and affects timesheets and balances.

leave_rule_id.description: Leave rule (leave type) id from deputy_query_resource with object LeaveRules.

location_id.description: Location (Company) id the leave applies to.

start.description: Start as Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: End as Unix timestamp in seconds.

tools.name: deputy_update_leave
tools.description: Approve, decline or cancel a leave request (Status), or change its dates and comment. Only the fields sent change.

tools.name: deputy_add_unavailability
tools.description: Record when an employee cannot work, once or repeating (e.g. every second Monday).

start.description: Start as Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: End as Unix timestamp in seconds.

recurrence.description: Repeat rule, e.g. {"FREQ":"WEEKLY","INTERVAL":2,"BYDAY":"MO"}. Omit for a one-off period.

tools.name: deputy_save_shift
tools.description: Add a shift, or update one when roster_id is given. Publishing (publish true) can notify the employee. The answer body is empty on success.

roster_id.description: Roster (shift) id to update; omit to add a new shift.

start.description: Start as Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: End as Unix timestamp in seconds.

employee_id.description: Employee id to assign; 0 or omitted with open 1 for an open shift.

publish.description: true publishes the shift (may notify the employee).

open.description: 1 shows the shift as open for anyone to claim, 0 not.

force_overwrite.description: 1 overwrites a clashing existing shift, 0 (default) does not.

confirm_status.description: 1 marks the shift as confirmed, 0 not.

tools.name: deputy_publish_rosters
tools.description: Publish shifts so employees see them, with the chosen notification.

notify.description: 1 SMS and email, 2 SMS, 3 email, 4 none, 5 ask employees to confirm.

all_locations.description: 1 publishes across all locations in this request, 0 only the given shifts' location.

tools.name: deputy_copy_rosters
tools.description: Copy the shifts of a date range of some areas forward (e.g. last week to this week).

from_date.description: Start of the source range, YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the source range, YYYY-MM-DD.

area_ids.description: Area (operational unit) ids whose shifts are copied.

error_details.description: 1 returns details about shifts that could not be copied.

tools.name: deputy_discard_rosters
tools.description: Discard (remove) shifts from the schedule. Cannot be undone; switched off at install.

tools.name: deputy_start_timesheet
tools.description: Clock an employee on in an area now: starts a running timesheet for them.

tools.name: deputy_end_timesheet
tools.description: Clock an employee off (ends a running timesheet), with an optional unscheduled meal break.

meal_break_minutes.description: Meal break minutes taken; 0 when none.

tools.name: deputy_pause_timesheet
tools.description: Start or end a break on a running timesheet (calling it again ends the break).

tools.name: deputy_save_timesheet
tools.description: Create a finished timesheet, or update one when timesheet_id is given: times, area, breaks and comment, optionally approved at once.

timesheet_id.description: Timesheet id to update; omit to create.

start.description: Start as Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: End as Unix timestamp in seconds.

slots.description: Breaks with times, as Deputy's Slots, e.g. [{"blnEmptySlot":false,"strType":"B","intUnixStart":1616367600,"intUnixEnd":1616369400,"mixedActivity":{"intState":2,"blnCanStartEarly":1,"blnCanEndEarly":1,"blnIsMandatory":1,"strBreakType":"M"}}].

roster_id.description: Shift (roster) id the timesheet belongs to.

tools.name: deputy_approve_timesheet
tools.description: Approve a timesheet (time approval) so it can be exported to payroll.

tools.name: deputy_discard_timesheet
tools.description: Discard a timesheet so it is not paid. Cannot be undone; switched off at install.

tools.name: deputy_post_memo
tools.description: Post a memo to the news feed of a location, optionally to selected locations or users, and optionally asking them to confirm they read it.

location_id.description: Location (Company) id that posts the memo.

location_ids.description: Location ids that receive the memo.

user_ids.description: User ids (not employee ids) that receive the memo.
